overhead.note: fixed per-call cost: autograd bookkeeping, argument packing, kernel dispatch

timing.note: forward_gbs and backward_gbs count the stream the naive mapping reads: both rows of every pair (forward) and every partner row plus that pair's grad and dist, once per destination row (backward). Both exceed copy_floor_gbs several-fold because the input is small enough to be served from cache, and the tiled forward moves far less than the stream figure implies. copy_floor_gbs is a copy of the same size on the same batch, so it is the device bandwidth the box was delivering at that moment.

notes: ATen selects pdist branches in a different order forward and backward: the forward tests isinf before the general formula, the backward tests p < 2 first, so p == -inf is a maximum forward and the p < 2 quotient backward. pdist rejects negative p, so a direct aten call is the only way in.
d == 0 returns zeros on both sides because ATen fills the packed vector; the kernel is not launched.
_pdist_backward requires n*(n-1)/2 values in grad_output and pdist; ATen reads out of bounds here, so the overlay raises instead.
A strided input to the aten ops is copied rather than rejected; public pdist makes the input contiguous first, so only a direct aten call differs.
float32 only: ATen's pdist kernels raise NotImplementedError for half and bfloat16 and MPS has no float64, so the dtype contract matches the CPU backend.

NaN and infinity propagate through the same branch as ATen: a NaN difference poisons p == 0, p == inf (the maximum is taken on the IEEE bit pattern) and every general p, and it poisons the p == 1 and p == inf gradients through sign(diff) even where the mask is zero.
Forward differences against CPU are float32 rounding behind a pairwise simd_sum; against float64 the MPS kernel is the closer of the two at large d.

Timing runs under a tier-1 lease on a box where a couple of dozen other probes share the GPU, so absolute times swing by several times between sweeps. Every candidate in a row - forward, backward, autograd step, and a copy of the same size - is timed round-robin inside the same batch, and the minima are compared: a minimum is a launch that did not have to wait, and comparing minima from the same batch is the only comparison that holds while the box is loaded. copy_floor_gbs states what the device was actually delivering in that batch.

The forward's tiled path applies when d is a multiple of 4, a row fits in eight float4 per lane, there are at least TILE_MIN_ROWS rows, and p is not in the general branch; the backward always runs its hoisted, four-way-unrolled sweep. Measured within single batches at 4096x256, the backward went 23.3 ms to 9.4 ms at p == 2 (2.5x), 17.2 to 7.3 at p == inf (2.4x) and 95.0 to 50.3 at p == 3 (1.9x), and the forward 6.19 to 3.84 ms at p == 2 (1.6x) and 3.75 to 2.08 at p == inf (1.8x).

A 2x3 forward is pure fixed cost - autograd bookkeeping, argument packing, dispatch - and measured 72 us on MPS against 0.8 us on the CPU kernel. Inputs below a few hundred rows are dispatch-bound and the CPU kernel wins on wall time there.

The kernels win once there is work to amortise the launch: at 4096x256 the forward is 15x the CPU kernel and the backward 69x at p == 2, and the general branch (p == 3), where the CPU spends four pow calls per element, is 51x forward and 122x backward. The spread across p is how much arithmetic each pair's term costs.

Forward allocation equals the packed output exactly (2 MiB at 1024x128, 128 MiB at 8192x32) against 0.5 GiB and 8 GiB for an n x n x d difference tensor; the 8192-row case runs inside the tier-1 2 GB lease, which 8 GiB would not.
